{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZWRcYw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhC9nGw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 35, "title": "Implement Ap real-mode LGDT/SGDT as a protected-mode prerequisite", "body": "## Problem

The Ap CPU cannot load or inspect the global descriptor table register, blocking a prerequisite for DOS-extender protected-mode initialization.

At baseline `1c9dcf67d23827f7ed62609affdea6f9c33f5c10`, [Cpu](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/1c9dcf67d23827f7ed62609affdea6f9c33f5c10/src/cpu.rs#L25) has no GDTR state. Its `extended` decoder has no `0F 01` implementation, so LGDT/SGDT stop execution with an unsupported-opcode error. Existing [CPU tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/1c9dcf67d23827f7ed62609affdea6f9c33f5c10/tests/cpu386.rs) cover real-mode addressing, faults and CPULEVEL, but provide no GDTR acceptance.

## Expected outcome

Implement only Ap real-mode GDTR loading and readback, using original Rust:

- `LGDT m`: `0F 01 /2`. Load the little-endian limit from bytes 0–1. With 16-bit operand size, load the 24-bit base from bytes 2–4 and clear its upper byte; with `66h`, load all four base bytes. The stored base is linear-address metadata, retained independently of installed RAM and A20. Loading it does not access the referenced descriptor table.
- `SGDT m`: `0F 01 /0`. Store a six-byte operand containing the 16-bit limit followed by the full 32-bit base, with either operand size. In particular, default-size SGDT after a 32-bit LGDT must preserve a nonzero high base byte.
- Support existing 16/32-bit effective-address decoding, SIB and segment overrides independently of operand size. Successful instructions preserve flags and general/segment registers.

LGDT semantics follow Intel's [Intel486 Programmer’s Reference Manual, pp. 26-193–194](https://manuals.plus/m/d86207aaebd9b10464f2058efc61559e6141d3b072db100e89bfe17c8187e143). That page also specifies full-base stores, although older SGDT descriptions and compatibility notes are inconsistent. Use the explicit full-32-bit store operation in Intel's [SDM, SGDT entry](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/835757/325383-sdm-vol-2abcd.pdf), and document this distinction.

Register operands raise guest invalid-opcode exception 6. LOCK is invalid. For these instructions, use the i486 manual's real-address-mode exception contract: any portion of the six-byte operand outside offsets `0000h–FFFFh` raises exception 13, including SS-selected operands. Preflight the complete operand before changing GDTR or writing destination bytes. Deliver restartable faults through the existing real-mode mechanism. Sources: Intel486 manual, pp. 26-194 and 26-261; [Intel SDM, SGDT exception table](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/782151/253667-sdm-vol-2b.pdf).

Keep GDTR state per CPU instance. Choose and document a deterministic emulator reset value; the i486 manual §10.1 explicitly leaves power-up GDTR undefined. Do not present that policy as a hardware reset guarantee.

Scope excludes LIDT/SIDT, CR0/PE transitions, descriptor lookup or validation, privilege changes, paging, task switching, FPU and Windows. VM retains its existing V30 decoding. Other `0F 01` operations must not silently succeed.

## Context and reproduction

A minimal Ap sequence is `0F 01 16 00 40` (`lgdt [4000h]`), followed by `0F 01 06 10 40` (`sgdt [4010h]`). With source bytes `34 12 78 56 34 12`, default-size LGDT loads limit `1234h`, base `00345678h`; prefixed LGDT loads base `12345678h`. Baseline execution stops at the first instruction.

Project progress: source inspection confirms #33/#34 added DMA controller-disable gating at scheduled FDC service time. The Coordinator reports 11 DMA tests, 111 native integration tests and 48 Chromium/Wasm tests passing, including baseline-negative checks and existing game regressions. The browser report used alternate ports after default-port startup failed. See [recorded validation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/1c9dcf67d23827f7ed62609affdea6f9c33f5c10/docs/validation.md#issue-33-dma-controller-disable). These are Coordinator-reported results; this evaluation ran no builds or tests. Supplied review/comment lists are empty, and no separate CI-success evidence was supplied. No open Issue is listed; recent completed improvements concern DMA.

All 26 inventory categories retain their supplied status and full required scope:

| Status | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| unimplemented | protected-mode, paging, fpu, rtc |
| implemented_unverified | ide, grcg, pcm86 |
| partial | cpu-v30, cpu386, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration |

This Issue completes only the GDTR instruction prerequisite. Remaining protected-mode work includes CR0 and entry/exit, descriptor tables and caches, segment validation, CPL and privilege transitions, interrupt/exception gates, and task-state behavior needed by DOS extenders. Paging and basic x87 retain their separate required scopes. Limited probes and six-game reports establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the specified Ap LGDT/SGDT behavior and per-instance GDTR state. Document the reset policy and specification distinctions above. Preserve VM behavior and explicit unsupported boundaries.
- [ ] Add original native tests in `tests/cpu386.rs`, named with a `gdtr_` prefix. `cargo test --locked --test cpu386 gdtr_` must cover both operand sizes crossed with both address sizes, representative SIB/default-SS addressing, segment overrides including FS/GS, unaligned operands, repeated overrides, exact six-byte stores and surrounding guards, unchanged flags/registers, independent CPU instances and Machine reset.
- [ ] Include a nonzero high base byte: 32-bit LGDT followed by both SGDT operand sizes must store it unchanged; subsequent 16-bit LGDT must clear it. Test zero/maximal limits and bases outside installed RAM without dereferencing them.
- [ ] Verify six-byte access boundaries: offset `FFFAh` succeeds; `FFFBh` and address-size-32 offsets beyond `FFFFh` fault before partial effects. Cover DS- and SS-selected operands, invalid register forms and LOCK. Assert exact exception vector, saved instruction-start IP including prefixes, restart behavior and unchanged GDTR/destination guards. Keep an initialized valid interrupt stack/vector table for these tests.
- [ ] Verify operand reads/writes use existing Bus mapping: distinguish A20-disabled/enabled source memory, preserve loaded base bits regardless of A20, and retain ROM write protection for SGDT destinations.
- [ ] Add an original MIT, source-built boot probe, for example `guest/gdtr.asm`, following existing offline assembly/image conventions. Record source/license, exact assembly command, source and image hashes, and execution budget in a fixture manifest; keep generated fixtures outside `web/`. The guest must check exact load/store results, guards and representative restartable faults, emitting distinct `GDTR PASS`/`GDTR FAIL` markers with bounded handlers and loops. No proprietary ROM or commercial guest is required.
- [ ] Execute the same probe image natively and through production release Wasm on Ap at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after emulator reset, within two million instruction slots per run. Assert PASS, absence of FAIL/errors and exact result/guard bytes; retain VM regressions. Demonstrate that at least one focused test and the probe fail on the unchanged baseline and pass with the implementation.
- [ ] The Coordinator performs the repository's README fixture preparation and checks: `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, media/font checks and `npm test`. Preserve existing CPULEVEL, hardware, DOS/application, VM, DMA and game assertions. Report exact commands, outcomes, provenance and any environment substitutions without skipped assertions or inflated compatibility claims.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
